newsitem.title: CHINA: China doesn't care about WTO entry - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: China doesn't care about WTO entry - newspaper.

text.p: After years of failed attempts to join the World Trade Organisation (WTO), China no longer cares whether it joins the global trade body, the China Daily on Tuesday quoted a senior customs official as saying.

"Accession or not, China has become indifferent and doesn't care any more," the official newspaper quoted Wu Jiahuang, director general of the tariffs department of China's General Administration of Customs, as saying.

China's past bid for entry to the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) and current attempts to join the WTO that succeeded it as the leading world trade club were like a "sunken boat" and an "ailing tree", Wu said.
China's senior leadership had concluded that negotiations with WTO members on the terms of its entry were politically tainted, the English-language newspaper quoted him as saying.
"In their anxiety to carve out markets in China, chief WTO member countries have ignored China's rightful reasons to protect its national industries," he said.

Beijing is seeking to join the WTO on the favourable terms accorded to developing countries, but some members -- with the United States most vocal among them -- have argued that China's economy is too large and powerful to be given such treatment.

Wu said Beijing was puzzled by the actions of developed countries such as the United States, European Union members and Canada that had imposed quotas on Chinese textile imports but would not allow China time to protect its own key industries.
Despite a decade of fruitless efforts to join GATT and the WTO, China had been able to expand its foreign trade and was no longer concerned about entry, he said.

"Fortunately, China's reform and opening have been strengthened over the last decade and China's foreign trade has expanded to 44 percent of gross national product last year," he said without giving details.
